StyleSphere: safe identity and payment state in a complex marketplace

A modular Spring Boot social-commerce platform combining content, recommendations, an AI shopping assistant, and transactions. My verified scope covered authentication, security, users, and simulated payment.

Background and goal

StyleSphere connects social discovery, short video and live content, recommendations, AI-assisted shopping, and e-commerce transactions. The transaction domain must keep orders, inventory, promotions, payment, and refunds consistent across complex states and concurrent actions.

Payment boundary: payment and settlement are simulated locally. The project does not connect to a live external gateway and does not collect real funds.

Technical challenges and solutions

Duplicate requests and conflicting results

Idempotency keys are isolated per user. Replaying the same key and payload returns the original result; changing the order or result returns an explicit HTTP 409, and terminal states cannot be rewritten.

Payment and cancellation races

A consistent lock order serialises cart, order, payment, inventory, and promotion operations so payment success cannot race with inventory release.

Partial failure across modules

Related writes join one READ_COMMITTED commerce transaction. Any persistence failure rolls back the unit and permits a safe retry.

Late asynchronous results

Provider facts are stored first and applied in a separate transaction. A late success after expiry or cancellation creates compensation instead of reactivating the order.

Validation result

The recorded backend batch contained 140 passing tests across payment, orders, promotions, products, and carts. Coverage included refunds, state races, permission revocation, rollback, idempotency, and persistence checks. This result describes a specific test batch and does not imply that a real payment gateway was integrated.
